_why: A floor typed from memory is a floor nobody can re-derive. These are the numbers the owner was shown on 2026-08-19 before she set the address floor at 0.30 address words per 100 words (26.995-COPY section C-9), written down so a later reader can CHECK the number instead of re-guessing it or quietly retuning it. Every value here was measured, none asserted. The sample set is small - twelve archived generations, three seeded examples, five arms from ticket #18 and one from #102 - and #18's own words apply to it: a threshold fitted to the same drafts that produced it is not validated by them. That is a stated limit of this calibration, not a defect in it.
_convention: D-35, and it is the reason this file exists in this shape: before believing any per-100-words finding on this phase, compute the numerator. Every ratio below is ADDRESS WORDS PER 100 WORDS - a rate, never a count. Where a count is meant it is named _count and is an integer. One finding on this map (#104's 'address falls on heavy evenings' slope) was already once a DENOMINATOR ARTIFACT: the absolute count of address words sat in a narrow band while length tripled, and the rate moved for that reason alone. A reader who mistakes one of these ratios for a count will reach the same wrong conclusion by the same route.
_property: The guarding property this calibration must keep, ASSERTED BY THE SUITE so a later edit cannot hollow it out. It has two halves now, because the owner deliberately moved the floor ABOVE writing she had accepted. ⚠ AMENDED 2026-08-21: THE EXCEPTION LIST IS NOW EMPTY. The one name it held was recorded on a ratio that was never a measurement of the shipped example (see _correction_2_the_fragments_row_was_never_a_cost), and no sample she accepted falls below this floor. The second half keeps its exception mechanism because that is the mechanism, not because a cost currently exists - and the prohibition on adding a name to it is unchanged and absolute. (1) The floor sits strictly above the impostor control - 0.30 against 0.18. (2) The floor sits at or below every sample she ACCEPTED, EXCEPT the ones named in what_the_floor_separates.accepted_samples_she_knowingly_gave_up, which she was shown and chose anyway. The exception is an explicit list of names, never a relaxation: if a later edit moves a number here so that the floor rejects any OTHER sample she accepted, or admits the impostor, the suite still fails and names which sample. Do not add a name to that list to make a suite go green - the list records a decision of hers, and growing it is a decision only she can make.
_no_writing_of_hers: EVERY VALUE IN THIS FILE IS A COUNT OR A RATIO. No sentence of hers, no title, no fragment of any reflection and no word of any draft appears anywhere in it - the arm labels are the names the tickets gave the arms, never quotations from them. Law 4 and D-16 applied: storing more of her writing than the job needs is a decision she makes deliberately, never a side effect of a test fixture. A machine check on this claim (the file contains no CJK character at all) is one of this plan's acceptance criteria, because that is the cheapest proof no fragment of her Chinese writing was pasted in. NOTE, so nobody conflates two different gates: this file lives under tests/fixtures/ and is OUTSIDE librarian/, so it does not touch the public-staging corpus pin and adding it must not move RECORDED_CORPUS_DIGEST.

floor._integer_spelling: The check compares integers on both sides (address_count * 10000 >= 30 * word_count) and divides nothing. 0.30 has no exact binary representation, so a float comparison would make 'a draft landing exactly on the floor passes' - which is a ruling - depend on which way the last bit fell.
floor._supersedes: 0.20, set by her earlier the SAME DAY and shipped for about an hour. The old number is recorded here rather than erased because the reason it moved is the point: she chose 0.20 on a FALSE DESCRIPTION of what it does. Section C-9's cost 3 told her '#102's turn-away arm at 0.295 fails a floor of 0.20', which is arithmetically wrong - 0.295 is ABOVE 0.20 and passed it. The claim had been true against the previously ruled ~0.3 and was carried across unchanged when the number moved. Shown the corrected table, she moved it back.
floor._the_part_that_is_not_hers: The resolution of '~0.3' to the machine value 0.30 is AN AGENT'S, not hers. 0.30 is the smallest value that catches the 0.295 turn-away arm, which is the case the floor exists for and her whole reason for moving the number; any looser resolution of '~0.3' would defeat her stated purpose. Recorded as a resolution rather than as her ruling, on the same convention as the abstain branch below - SHE MAY CORRECT IT.
floor._not_a_fine_instrument: The gap to the impostor control is 0.12 at this floor, and the gap to the case it was built for is 0.005. This is not precision the evidence can carry and must never be described as though it were. D-03's words hold unchanged: a floor against ONE failure mode, gameable, and never evidence that the writing is warm.

samples._all_ratios: address words per 100 words, measured, not asserted.
